## macOS: survive a change of VPN address

**Fix (macOS clients):** when the coordinator gave a macOS member a new VPN address (an edit in the console), the member could still receive traffic but everything it originated was dropped by its peers. macOS keeps the interface address a route was added under, so the existing network route went on sourcing packets from the old address, which peers reject as spoofed. A change of our own address now re-binds every route on the device to the new one. Linux members were not affected, since Linux picks the source address when it sends.

If a macOS member on 0.5.1 or older has already had its address changed, restarting it also clears the problem.

### Console
- **Address check** is a badge: green *dialable*, red *not dialable*, yellow *not probed*.
- **Routes** on a relay card: *internet exit* on its own line, then IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes as badges in separate groups.
- Every time is a full local timestamp with its UTC offset, e.g. `2026-09-26 14:05:07+08`: config versions, "as of", heartbeat and join times.
- **View** is renamed **Config Version**.
- A badge that changes state (behind → OK) switches at once instead of flashing.
- "Token secret last replaced …" is no longer shown on member cards. Take-overs by another machine still are.

**Compatibility:** no wire, token or config changes. 0.5.2 interoperates with 0.3.x–0.5.1 members. Update macOS clients; on Linux the update is optional. From 0.5.0 on: `sudo nqvpn-client --self-update`, then restart the service.

|---|---|---|
| Linux (static musl) | `nqvpn-0.5.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.2-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | `nqvpn-0.5.2-macos-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.2-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| FreeBSD | `nqvpn-0.5.2-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.2-freebsd-arm64.tar.gz` |
